note: Risk-off turn. S&P 500 closed 7,266.99 on Jun 10 (-1.62%), ~5.9% above its rising 200DMA (6,863) — the cushion is shrinking. The Dow fell ~953 pts (-1.87%) and the Nasdaq -1.98%; chips have led the slide after Broadcom's softer-than-hoped AI guidance (the Nasdaq's worst day since Apr 2025 came Jun 4 as ~$1T was wiped from semis). Two real drivers: a hotter-than-expected May CPI (+4.2% YoY, a 3-year high) and renewed Iran tension after President Trump signaled negotiations were taking 'too long' and threatened more action — pushing WTI to ~$90 and Brent to ~$93. Yield curve positive (10Y 4.52% vs 2Y 4.15%); the Fed is expected to hold the 3.50-3.75% range at the Jun 16-17 FOMC (effective ~3.63%). VIX has firmed back toward ~21 with the selloff. Leadership remains in Energy (+~22% YTD), Materials, Industrials and Consumer Staples while mega-cap tech/semis lag. Two of nine bear-checklist flags are up: active geopolitical risk and signs of mega-cap/tech distribution.
